  • C.11 Where not listed above, car parking is to be provided in accordance with Parramatta DCP 2023 or The Guide to Traffic Generating Developments, whichever is greater.
  • C.12 Car parking rates are a maximum and any excess parking may be counted as gross floor area.
  • C.13 Car parking rates should be rounded-up to the nearest whole number.

8.5.12.27 BICYCLE PARKING

Objectives

  • O.01 Ensure safe, accessible, and adequate bicycle parking is provided for residents and visitors of the precinct.

Controls

  • C.01 Ensure secure bicycle parking is provided for non-residential and residential uses.
  • C.02 Where possible, bicycle parking for residents and/or employees should be provided at-grade.
  • C.03 Where bicycle parking is provided within the basement or above ground levels, it is to be conveniently located.
  • C.04 Bicycle parking access and facilities are to be provided in accordance with the relevant Australian Standards and Part 6 - Traffic and Transport of the Parramatta DCP 2023.
  • C.05 Visitor bicycle parking shall be located conveniently within the building and is to be undercover and accessible at all times.
  • C.06 The number of bicycle parking is to be provided in accordance with Part 6 - Traffic and Transport of the Parramatta DCP 2023.

8.5.12.28 SUSTAINABILITY

Objectives

  • O.01 Increase energy efficiency.
  • O.02 Reduce reliance on potable water.
  • O.03 Deliver built forms and public open spaces which respond to winter sunlight and cooling summer breezes.
  • O.04 Reduce waste and increase the reuse and recycling of materials.
  • O.05 Encourage the use of electric vehicle car charging.

Controls

  • C.01 Residential development is to comply with BASIX requirements.
  • C.02 Public amenities are to use water and energy efficient fittings.
  • C.03 Provision of electric vehicle charging infrastructure is to be provided in accordance with Section 6.1.3 - Electric Vehicle Charing Infrastructure of the Parramatta DCP 2023.
  • C.04 Water sensitive design measures are to be integrated where possible, such as water re-use systems for irrigation.

URBAN HEAT ISLAND

8.5.12.29 VERTICAL FACADES

Objectives

  • O.01 Minimise the reflection of solar heat downward from the building façade into private open space or the public domain.
  • O.02 Where multiple reflective surfaces or convex geometry of reflective surface introduce the risk of focussing of solar reflections into the public spaces.
  • O.03 Solar heat reflections from any part of a building must not exceed 1,000W/m² in the public domain at any time.
  • O.04 A reflectivity modelling report may be required to qualify extent of reflected solar heat radiation.

8.5.12.30 AWNINGS

Objectives

  • O.01 Ensure awnings are designed to improve user comfort, providing shelter from the sun and reduced solar heat at the street level.

Controls

  • C.01 All awnings and shading devices should have non-reflective surfaces.
  • C.02 Transparent awnings are not encouraged on buildings. If transparent awnings are used, the awning must have a maximum solar transmittance of 50.

8.5.12.31 PUBLIC ART

Objectives

  • O.01 Enhance the sense of place through the provision of public art.
  • O.02 Use public art to enhance and define the character of the site and locality.

Controls

  • C.01 Public art is encouraged within the central public open space or through-site links, independent of building forms.
  • C.02 Public Art is to have a value of up to $50,000 and is to be integrated into the public open space.

8.5.13 NORTH ROCKS VILLAGE PRECINCT

This Section applies to 361-365 North Rocks Road, North Rocks as shown in Figure 8.5.13.1. Land application map and must be read in conjunction with any relevant Parts of the Parramatta DCP 2023. Where there are inconsistencies between the controls contained within this section and any other controls within this DCP, the North Rocks Village Precinct DCP provisions will prevail to the extent of the inconsistency.

Figure 8.5.13.1 - Land Application Map

8.5.13.1 DESIRED FUTURE CHARACTER

The site will deliver a Housing Diversity Precinct that will incorporate a mix of housing typologies including detached dwellings, terrace housing, seniors housing, aged care and residential flat buildings. Future medium density development at the North Rocks site must consider the arrangement and composition of new built form on a whole-of-site basis to create a central composition of higher density development that appropriately transitions to lower scale development responding to existing peripheral low density residential settings to the east and west. New buildings should achieve a high level of architectural design quality and resolution, using high quality and robust materials.

The site comprises existing significant landscape assets that can be retained as features of the new place, benefiting the amenity and experience of the new residential community. The generous proportions of the Primary Street and consistent building setbacks offer the opportunity to augment the existing tree canopy and consolidate a landscape setting for new buildings. The street layout and through site links provide permeability and connectivity. Community and public open spaces complement the landscape neighborhood character and provide desirable community facilities such as multisport court/s, playgrounds, oval, amenities building and a community centre.

General Objectives

  • O.01 Create a street network which provides safe and accessible vehicular and pedestrian access and movement through the site, which is compatible with the surrounding streets.
  • O.02 Provide for well-designed public open spaces and streets to optimise liveability, amenity, useability and walkability for the local community.
  • O.03 Provide a mixture of compatible non-residential uses and community uses, activating public open spaces and streets, improving the character of the locality.
  • O.04 Deliver a diversity of housing typologies, housing mix and affordability that are compatible with the scale of the locality.
  • O.05 Include provision for a well-located, accessible and prominent community facility, oval and sports facilities.
  • O.06 Development is designed to respond carefully to the topography, streetscape, existing trees and natural environment as key features.

8.5.13.2 SPATIAL STRUCTURE AND BUILT FORM

8.5.13.2.1 INDICATIVE SITE STRUCTURE

Objectives

  • O.01 Create a legible, pedestrianised public domain by sitting buildings to define the street network, open spaces and through-site links.
  • O.02 Create attractive, comfortable and inviting streetscapes for the local community.
  • O.03 Integrate the new streets and buildings within the existing street network, with a logical street hierarchy.
  • O.04 Minimise cut and fill across the site to maximise tree retention and to minimise impacts to adjoining properties, disruption to natural drainage lines and the need for retaining walls.
  • O.05 Ensure that FSR is equitably distributed across the precinct.
  • O.06 Ensure that the ground floor of buildings interface relates directly to adjacent street level.
  • O.07 Respond to the site's unique bushland setting, retain existing mature trees and provide deep soil to plant new trees.

Controls

  • C.01 The street layout, through-site links, open space, development sites and building footprints are to be consistent with the plan shown in Figure 8.5.13.2 and the established street hierarchy in Figure 8.5.13.5.
  • C.02 The street layout and building footprints must demonstrate viable retention of existing trees where possible, including clusters of significant trees.
  • C.03 A site wide Landscape Plan is required and demonstrate that the overall site can achieve a minimum of 40% tree canopy.
  • C.04 Building courtyards must prioritise a northern orientation for solar access.
  • C.05 A Concept and Stage 1 Infrastructure Development Application must confirm site levels, infrastructure and concept lot designs for the entire development site as a framework for future individual development lot assessments including:
  • vertical and horizontal alignments for road reservation, park and development lot boundaries,
  • a site wide earthworks, grading and stormwater design that minimises cut and fill, provides suitable gradients for street and block development and confirms existing individual tree retention,
  • how retention of significant existing trees is maximised, and
  • C.06 Indicative building envelopes and lot by lot FSR.
  • C.07 Individual development lot applications must demonstrate consistency with the above approved Concept and Stage 1 Development Application confirming:
  • proposed site and road levels follow natural ground level as much as possible,
  • where retaining walls are proposed there is no alternative,
  • levels disparity across and between adjacent blocks and buildings is minimised,
  • ground floor units are not below the adjacent street level,
  • building floor levels and entries interface smoothly with all street frontages, and
  • development on the subject lot does not compromise the ability of neighbouring lots and the rest of the site to achieve the same objectives.

Figure 8.5.13.2 - Indicative site layout

8.5.13.2.2 SETBACKS

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide adequate setbacks that provide for a comfortable public domain, with adequate sunlight, and an appropriate scale relationship with the street.
  • O.02 Create a clear and consistent delineation between public and private spaces and landscape interface between building and streets.
  • O.03 Maximise the area for landscape embellishment and buffer to all buildings fronting public streets.
  • O.04 Confirm a consistent alignment of buildings and basement car parks for all streets.
  • O.05 Provide a deep soil zone around the periphery of all development sites that are contiguous with road reservations and open space areas.

Controls

  • C.01 Minimum ground level building and basement setbacks are to be provided in accordance with Figure 8.5.13.3.
  • C.02 Council's preferred setback on the east west road is 6m; however a reduced setback may be considered to not less than 4m provided it can be demonstrated that the existing trees will be retained, and new trees can grow to their full capacity; and overshadowing of oval is not reduced.
  • C.03 Provide understorey planting to all landscape setback zones.
  • C.04 Provide small trees (6-8m), and medium sized trees (10-12m) in all landscape setback zones that are 4m wide, or more than 4m wide, respectively. Small trees minimum 3m from the building line, medium trees minimum 4m away from the building line.
  • C.05 Basements are not to encroach into setback areas.
  • C.06 Design buildings in a way that minimises the need for structures such as ramps, retaining walls, steps and other hardscape elements within the landscape setback zone.
  • C.07 Basement ramps and entries are to be wholly located within the building footprint and not within the setback zone.
  • C.08 Electrical pillars, fire hydrants and other services are to be carefully designed so that they are visually recessive in the building façade and/or landscape setbacks and that do not pose an obstruction to pedestrians. All Development Application drawings must clearly demonstrate how the placement and design of these elements has been thoughtfully and successfully resolved.
  • C.09 The provision of upper level building setbacks is based on streetscape analysis to determine what is appropriate to reduce perceived bulk and height of buildings. Where proposed, the minimum upper level setback must be 3m.

Figure 8.5.13.3 - Minimum basement and ground level building setbacks

8.5.13.2.3 BUILDING HEIGHT

Objectives

  • O.01 Building heights that respond to the topography and deliver appropriate transitions to surrounding development. Taller buildings are to be located at the centre of the site transitioning in height down to existing lower scale, surrounding built form, bushland areas and street interfaces.
  • O.02 Ensure that building forms allow for a high level of solar access to buildings and the public domain within and outside the development site.

Controls

  • C.01 The maximum building height must correspond in storeys as follows:
Metres (as per the LEP)Maximum number of storeys
9m2
12m3
14m3
23m6
  • C.02 Roof plant, services and rooftop structures (such as pergolas or shelters) which provide protection to the communal open spaces are to be excluded from the calculation of storeys. These elements must be integrated into the design of the building.

8.5.13.2.4 BUILDING DESIGN

Objectives

  • O.01 Ensure sites are of a sufficient width to achieve a safe and efficient pedestrian and vehicular access.
  • O.02 Deliver high amenity, interest and visual appeal in the street environment with views between buildings to the bushland and open spaces
  • O.03 Minimise the perception of visual bulk and scale of the development.
  • O.04 Ensure building materials contribute positively to the streetscape, are sustainable, durable, and easy to maintain.

Controls

  • C.01 For new subdivisions for dwelling houses a development must have a minimum site frontage width of 12 metres.
  • C.02 Provide minor breaks in the built form to reduce perceived building bulk and provide views and to and from internal courtyards.
  • C.03 A maximum of one step in the built form between any podium and upper-level typology is to be provided.
  • C.04 Any part of a basement or sub-floor that projects more than 1m above natural ground level comprises a storey.
  • C.05 Buildings are to incorporate a range of high-quality, sustainable and durable materials in a range of compatible colours and textures.
  • C.06 The building must:
  • be modulated vertically in segments that relate to a fine-grain subdivision pattern where the site frontage is more than 25m.
  • be of predominantly masonry character with lightweight panel construction or curtain walling.
  • be articulated with depth, relief and shadow on the street facade. A minimum relief of 150mm between the masonry finish and glazing face must be achieved.
  • utilise legible architectural elements and spatial types - doors, windows, pilasters, sills, plinths and infill etc, not necessarily expressed in a literal traditional manner.
  • C.07 The following buildings are to have splayed corners:
  • SW corner Lot A-4
  • NW corner Lot A-8, and
  • NE corner Lot A-Z

8.5.13.2.5 BUILDING RESPONSE TO TOPOGRAPHY

Objectives

  • O.01 Site designs to avoid the need for excessive cut and fill, boundary walls or other retaining walls in setback areas, and/or excessive vertical circulation between ground floor and external areas.
  • O.02 Deliver a ground floor that achieves amenity and privacy for residents while providing passive surveillance and engagement with the street.
  • O.03 Locate apartments at or above the street level to facilitate sunlight access, safety, privacy and a suitable streetscape interface.
  • O.04 Seamlessly integrate accessibility into the design of buildings and landscaping in a way that does not dominate the setback areas.
  • O.05 Maximise deep soil and green landscape area in the setback areas providing a dominant landscape setting for new buildings.

Controls

  • C.01 Match building design to suit the degree of slope, using split slab construction to either take up the slope of the site with additional half levels or step to complement the slope.
  • C.02 Ground floor apartments must be between 500mm and 900mm above street level where there is a narrow 3m setback.
  • C.03 Only a small proportion of ground floor apartments are permitted below ground level to address the slope of the land. These apartments are to be a maximum 500mm below street level only.
  • C.04 Where apartments are located below the street level, the following applies:
  • Adequate solar access to habitable rooms and private open space must be demonstrated. A minimum floor-to-ceiling height of 3.1 metres must be provided to ensure adequate solar access.
  • Adequate privacy screening and landscaping must be demonstrated.
  • C.05 Ground floor apartments facing the street must have individual apartment entries where feasible.
  • C.06 Buildings must be designed to provide passive surveillance to open space and through site links by minimising blank walls and non-habitable uses to these spaces.
  • C.07 Public and privately owned land must be clearly delineated at all interfaces with streets and open spaces.
  • C.08 Where a basement breaches the natural ground level, it must be contained within the building footprint.
  • C.11 Where appropriate, vertical circulation must be located within the building envelope to prevent impacts on landscaping and ensure a clear relationship between the building entry and the street.
  • C.12 Retaining walls within the development site shall be avoided or minimised. Where they are required, retaining walls must have a maximum height of 1m, designed to blend with the individual development including materials and expression, and be built of high quality, robust and durable materials. Suitable materials include natural stone and/or concrete - natural concrete or, with integral colour.

8.5.13.2.6 RETAIL GROUND FLOOR FRONTAGE

Objectives

  • O.01 Ensure retail frontages provide comfort, shelter and amenity for pedestrians.
  • O.02 Provide an active ground floor frontage that is visually interesting, accessible and integrated with the design of the public domain.
  • O.03 Maintain complementary architectural detail.

Controls

  • C.01 Ground floor retail space and active frontages are to be generally located per Figure 8.5.13.4.
  • C.02 Ground floor commercial and retail uses must be appropriately located to activate the public domain.
  • C.03 Services, substations, loading docks and driveways on building frontages must be minimised to reduce inactive walls.
  • C.04 Electrical pillars, fire hydrants and other services are to be designed so that they are visually recessive in the building façade.
  • C.05 Awnings must be provided where active non-residential frontages are proposed.
  • C.06 Awnings must complement the architectural character of the building.
  • C.07 Awnings must have a minimum depth of 2m, unless street trees are provided.

Figure 8.5.13.4 - Indicative Non Residential Use and Active Frontage

8.5.13.2.7 RESIDENTIAL DESIGN APARTMENT QUALITY

Objectives

  • O.01 Ensure development achieves good amenity standards for residents.

Controls

  • C.01 Where practicable, balconies must be rectangular in shape with the longer side parallel to the facade of the building.
  • C.02 Apartment design must incorporate suitable spaces that can be utilised as a work-from-home space.
  • C.03 Minimum floor-to-floor heights for residential apartments are to be 3.2m for all levels.

8.5.13.2.8 COMMUNITY CENTRE

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide a prominent, accessible, and appropriately located community facility that meets the needs of the North Rocks community and visitors.
  • O.02 Create a vibrant facility that is integrated into the adjacent public domain areas.
  • O.03 Ensure all levels of the community facility overlook the Village Square.
  • O.04 Ensure that floor heights support a range of uses and provide appropriate amenity.
  • O.05 The building is to be designed to have access to daylight.
  • O.06 Ensure the interior layout is programmable, flexible and open plan.
  • O.07 Incorporate best practice sustainability principles and standards into the design of the building and operation of the facility.

Controls

  • C.01 The facility is to be located in the building generally as shown in Figure 8.5.13.4
  • C.02 The facility must provide a primary, clearly identifiable entry addressing the new village square. A secondary entry must also be provided, either facing the oval or along North Rocks Road.
  • C.03 Building services and fire exits are to be minimised. Where practical, services are to be located away from the Village Square and not directly facing it.
  • C.04 Provide an outlook to the Village Square and oval to all levels of the Community Centre.
  • C.05 Minimum floor-to-floor heights shall be provided as follows:
  • Ground floor 4.5m and a minimum of 3.8m for all levels above.
  • C.06 No portion of the community centre is to be below ground level except for the basement carparking.
  • C.07 The interior spaces of the community centre are to be open plan and free from columns where possible.
  • C.08 Building design must incorporate high-quality materials and finishes including masonry highlights using natural materials and be of high sustainability value.

8.5.13.2.9 EXISTING COTTAGE

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide a prominent, accessible, and appropriately located community facility that meets the needs of the North Rocks community and visitors.
  • O.02 Incorporate best practice sustainability principles and standards into the design of the building and operation of the facility.

Controls

  • C.01 The facility is to be located in the building per Figure 8.5.13.4.
  • C.02 The existing cottage community facility is to open out onto a garden with passive seating.
  • C.03 Building design must incorporate high quality materials and finishes including masonry highlights using natural materials and be of high sustainability value.

8.5.13.2.10 LANDSCAPE DESIGN AND PLANTING

Objectives

  • O.01 Improve amenity of new neighbourhoods through the provision of landscaping on development lots.
  • O.02 Establish a variety of vegetation types and species, especially tree canopy cover.
  • O.03 Provide successful landscaped boundary setbacks and communal open space to enhance and soften street presentation, screen buildings, provide ground level amenity and suitable separation to neighbours.
  • O.04 Assist with the management of water and urban cooling.

Controls

  • C.01 A minimum 15 % of all land zoned R4 High Density Residential is to be provided as deep soil.
  • C.02 A minimum dimension of 6 metres is required for part of the deep soil zone, equal to at least 7% of the total site area.
  • C.03 The remaining deep soil zone may be provided with a minimum dimension of 4 metres x 4 metres.
  • C.04 A Landscape Plan must be provided for all landscape areas including landscape setbacks, courtyards and other communal open spaces and must demonstrate that the overall site achieves 40% canopy cover.
  • C.05 Canopy vegetation must be provided in the street frontage setbacks.
  • C.06 Built form configurations should allow for the embellishment of ground level communal courtyard open spaces with 40% canopy tree cover and generous understorey landscaping that is healthy, thriving , sustainable and easy to maintain over the long term.
  • C.07 For residential flat buildings, each development lot must provide a central courtyard communal open space at ground level.
  • C.08 Where basements extend beneath communal courtyards, the top of slab must be below ground level allowing for a minimum soil depth of 1.2 metres to support landscaping including trees. This area will not contribute to deep soil zone calculations and must provide appropriate soil conditions, including automatic irrigation and drainage, for planting above structures.
  • C.09 Tree planting and landscaping located on a slab must achieve soil depth and volume per Apartment Design Guidelines requirements. Canopy trees are to be planted at ground level.
  • C.10 Soft landscape embankment gradients must be no more than 1:5.
  • C.11 All open space shall reflect the principles of 'Safer by Design' (Crime Prevention through Environmental Design - CPTED) by minimising high retaining walls, dense planting and ensuring casual surveillance of communal areas from both residential and non-residential uses.
  • C.12 Augment existing tree planting in the 10m landscape buffer fronting North Rocks Road to serve as street trees and to screen the new development. Minimise earthworks and level changes for the full width of this zone. Duplication of road access or any major hard landscaping including underground utility services is not permitted.
  • C.13 Minimise impervious surfaces and major earthworks or level changes in all landscape setback areas.

8.5.13.3 PUBLIC DOMAIN

8.5.13.3.1 STREET NETWORK, SITE ACCESS AND FOOTPATHS

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide a safe, efficient, and generous network for pedestrian and bicycle movements as well as vehicular access.
  • O.02 Create shady, attractive and comfortable streetscapes for the local community.
  • O.03 Maximise two-way vehicular traffic flow and to allow for on-street parking.
  • O.04 Directly integrate the new development with the existing street network.
  • O.05 Ensure that Council's design and construction requirements for public streets are met.
  • O.06 Ensure consistency with Parramatta Bike Plan and Parramatta Ways Walking Strategy.

Controls

  • C.01 Public Domain Alignment plans are to be submitted with any development application detailing proposed alignments and works on land owned by, or to be dedicated to Council. The scope of work must include the North Rocks Road public footpath fronting the development. The plans are to be prepared in accordance with the requirements of the Parramatta Public Domain Guidelines.
  • C.02 The design of the internal roads must be in accordance with Council's design and construction standards, the relevant Australian Standards, Austroads Guidelines and TfNSW Technical Directions.
  • C.03 On-street parking is to be provided where available within the proposed road network.
  • C.04 Public footpath widths are to be minimum 1.5m-1.8m wide consistent with street sections.
  • C.05 Footpaths are to be provided in front of all residential apartment buildings at the interface with a proposed publicly accessible open space. Paths should be located outside the landscaped building setback, to aid in wayfinding and to delineate between private and public spaces.
  • C.06 Raised pedestrian/cycle priority crossings are required to access community and retail facilities.
  • C.07 Street trees are required at regular centres, typically 8-10m, for both sides of new internal streets.
  • C.08 The proposed extent and type of cycle access throughout the development is to be generally in accordance with Figure 8.5.13.16. Provide on-road mixed traffic cycle access on all internal streets in the development.
  • C.09 Provide a 3m shared path on North Rocks Road public footpath measured from back of kerb.

8.5.13.3.2 PUBLIC AND PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE OPEN SPACE

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide high quality public spaces and pedestrian connections that improve the quality of the site and its relationship with the surrounding locality.
  • O.02 Deliver sustainable, robust, useable, flexible and adaptable open spaces which have the capacity to support a variety of recreational uses and activities.
  • O.03 Provide a network of publicly accessible open spaces that allow preservation of substantial existing significant tree vegetation and to maximise the amenity of the new development.
  • O.04 Provide through-site links which improve walkability and permeability and relate to the surrounding locality.
  • O.05 Provide a fit-for-purpose full size multi-use playing field with a suitable playing surface, associated sporting infrastructure, play spaces and other community facilities and amenities suitable to service the new development.
  • O.06 Provide a new village square associated with the community centre and retail precinct.
  • O.07 Augment existing large trees and establish a substantial tree canopy across the site in line with State Government canopy targets.
  • O.08 Create development interfaces to public open spaces that are safe, accessible, activated and offer a high level of casual surveillance.

Controls

  • C.01 Public and publicly accessible open spaces are to be provided in accordance with Figure 8.5.13.17.
  • C.02 The designs for the public and publicly accessible open spaces are to be developed in consultation with Council. They are to be designed to:
  • Incorporate a palette of high quality and durable materials, and robust and drought tolerant landscaping species.
  • Include clear, accessible, safe, and convenient linkages to each other, to surrounding buildings, and to the public open space network.
  • Integrate stormwater management and water sensitive urban design that protects recreational functionality.
  • Include design elements, furniture, and infrastructure to facilitate active and passive recreation, relaxation and social interaction.
  • Maximise the safety and security of users consistent with 'Safety by Design' (CPTED) principles.
  • Encourage pedestrian use through the design of open space pathways and entrances.
  • Clearly delineate private and publicly accessible open spaces where there is a direct interface.
  • Incorporate appropriate levels of lighting to maximise hours of use in a way that does not create nuisance to surrounding residents or impact nocturnal ecology.
  • Accommodate high levels of use and diverse recreational needs.
  • C.03 Where retaining walls are required, they must have maximum height of 1m and be built of high quality robust and durable materials. Suitable materials include natural stone or other masonry, or concrete, preferably in-situ concrete. For Council parks applied external facings, render or painted finishes are not permissible.
  • C.04 Solar access to public open spaces:
  • 100% solar access to the oval for a minimum of 5 hours daily at the winter solstice (excluding shade from trees) is to be achieved. Minor overshadowing will only be considered where it does not adversely impact the playing surface.
  • 50% solar access to all other public park spaces for a minimum of 5 hours daily at the winter solstice (excluding shade from trees) is to be achieved.
  • 4 hours solar access to playgrounds in the winter solstice (excluding shade from trees) is to be achieved.
  • Solar access to all other community open spaces is to be maximised.

C.05 Shade:

  • Tree planting must include numerous large canopy trees (15-20m mature height, minimum 100L at planting) contributing to summer shade and urban heart mitigation.
  • Achieve 20% protection from direct sunlight at the summer solstice to reduce ultraviolet radiation exposure (excluding the oval).

Oval

  • C.06 The oval must be set at a level to reduce retaining walls and cut and fill.
  • C.07 The oval must have a visible accessible path access from North Rocks Road between the oval and the Community Centre to the internal street network, and from the north west corner of the oval.
  • C.08 The oval must have floodlighting and irrigation to maximise capacity and allow for extended hours of community use as per Council's Sportsground Strategy.
  • C.09 Provide multi-purpose courts in the area adjoining the oval, which can be used for sports including pickleball, basketball, futsal, netball, tennis at a size of 32m x 40m with a 1.5m buffer.
  • C.10 The multisport courts must be serviced by a clear accessible path from the local street network.
  • C.11 Provide a pedestrian footpath and 3m wide screen planting to clearly delineate the western and southern boundaries of the residential development lot A-6.
  • C.12 Provide a minimum 6m separation/setback between the boundary of lot A-6 and the multisport courts. (Note: Lot A-6 includes the terrace housing on the northern perimeter of the oval).

Figure 8.5.13.17 - Public Open Space Plan (Note: Bushland area is subject to an Asset Protection Zone and Rural Fire Service requirements).

  • C.13 The space is to be attractive and provide high levels of amenity that consider climate, safety, activity, circulation, seating, lighting, and enclosure.
  • C.14 The oval must be provided with a circuit path around the circumference for walking and access as required to service future maintenance and operations.

Village Square

  • C.15 Provide a visible, prominent, accessible path from the Village Square to the oval.

Publicly Accessible Open Spaces Including Through-Site Links

  • C.16 Privately owned but publicly accessible open spaces include linear parks and through-site links that are proposed as part of the development. Proposed publicly accessible open spaces must allow for the retention of significant existing trees, amenity and general embellishment of the development
  • C.17 Publicly accessible open spaces must provide a 24/7 public access easement.
  • C.18 Provide safe, equitable pedestrian access whilst also incorporating passive recreational uses such as seating, lighting, and general landscape embellishments.
  • C.19 Provide clear delineation of public and privately accessible land at the edges of the links and community open spaces. Provide a pedestrian footpath delineation and fencing where community open spaces interface with private properties. Provide suitable privacy for any ground floor residential interface at the edges.

North East Park

  • C.20 Parkland area to include a passive seating area and may incorporate community gardening opportunities and appropriate supporting infrastructure where feasible and appropriate to the context.
  • C.21 Provide a vegetated buffer screen to the residential interface.
  • C.22 Structures below existing high voltage powerlines to be restricted in height.

Bushland Reserve

  • C.23 Provide a bushwalking track to provide opportunities for interaction with nature.

8.5.13.3.3 OVERHEAD POWERLINES

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide a desirable outlook for all above ground dwellings in the development and maximise opportunity for tree planting.

Controls

  • C.01 New power supply servicing the development, including street lighting, is to be undergrounded.
  • C.02 Existing overhead power lines on the north side of North Rocks Road are to be undergrounded as part of the development.

8.5.13.3.4 STREET TREES

Objectives

  • O.01 Include the provision of new street trees to improve the character of the public domain.
  • O.02 Improve and enhance environmental biodiversity, provide shade, and mitigate temperature at ground level.
  • O.03 Improve visual amenity of the public domain and from the buildings.

Controls

  • C.01 Street trees are required at regular centres, preferably 8-10m for both sides of each new internal street.
  • C.02 Street trees to be a minimum 100L at planting.
  • C.03 Design drawings must identify a zone below ground level, free of new services, reserved for tree planting, in all new streets.
  • C.04 Street trees along North Rocks Road are to be planted in the private setback in a consistent 'avenue' alignment to augment existing tree planting. Existing trees are to be retained. Tree size are to be large (15-20m at maturity) and minimum 200L at planting.

8.5.13.4 VEHICULAR ACCESS AND PARKING

8.5.13.4.1 VEHICULAR ACCESS TO DEVELOPMENT LOTS

Objectives

  • O.01 The amount, location and design of car parking cater for the needs of residents, workers and visitors.
  • O.02 The impact of vehicle access points and driveways on the streetscape, pedestrian safety and quality of the public domain is minimised.

Controls

  • C.01 Where practicable, there must be only one vehicular entry point per block.
  • C.02 Vehicular access must be provided at the lowest point of the street frontage.
  • C.03 Where practicable, basement access must be located on local secondary streets.
  • C.04 Locate vehicular driveways where they minimise the need for steep ramping from the street, so that the visual impact of driveways is minimised.
  • C.05 Vehicular access doors must be fitted behind the façade and finished of a material that will integrate into the building.
  • C.06 Vehicle access must be designed to minimise the visual impact to the street.
  • C.07 Vehicle access must be located a minimum of 10 metres from the perpendicular of any intersection of any two roads.
  • C.08 All vehicles must enter and exit the site in a forward direction.
  • C.09 Vehicle and pedestrian access must be appropriately separated to remove conflict.
  • C.10 Loading dock and waste collection must be incorporated within the building envelopes and must be located within the basement with one entry where possible.

8.5.13.4.2 ON-SITE DEVELOPMENT PARKING

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide an appropriate amount of parking for the development.
  • O.02 Minimise the negative impact of underground car park basement entries.
  • O.03 Ensure adequate on-site car parking is provided for the facility that can be separately and easily managed and operated by Council.

Controls

  • C.01 Adequate landscaped area must be maintained around the basement footprints.
  • C.02 Car parking for non-residential uses are to be provided as set-out below.
  • C.03 A traffic impact assessment must demonstrate that the proposed parking is sufficient to support the oval and community facility uses.
  • C.04 On-Street car parking within the immediate street adjoining the oval and community facility maybe used to satsify parking demand for the oval and community facility only.
  • C.05 Car parking for all other uses are to be provided in accordance with Part 6 of the Parramatta Development Control Plan (refer to Table 6.2.1).
  • C.06 Car parking rates must be rounded-up to the nearest whole number.
FacilityMinimum car parking provision
Oval30 spaces
Community Facility15 spaces or 1 space per 100sqm

PARRAMATTA AND GRANVILLE

The increase in population associated with higher density development makes it necessary for wider carriageways and footpaths to cater for the increase in vehicular and pedestrian traffic. Therefore, to achieve a more consistent road width and a more efficient road system, Council requires in those areas of higher density development, that a strip of land be dedicated for road widening.

This Section of this DCP provides provisions to guide development and ensure appropriate measures are taken to support Road Widenings, Road Closures and Splay Corners In and Adjacent To Residential R4 Zones within Parramatta and Granville. These are shown in Figure 8.5.14.14, Figure 8.5.14.15 and Figure 8.5.14.16.

Objectives

  • O.01 Provide controls for road widening, road closures and splay corners.
  • O.02 Achieve a more consistent carriageway width along the length of nominated roads.
  • O.03 Achieve a more efficient road system in those areas of higher density development associated with the increase in population.
  • O.04 Provide wider carriageways and footpaths to cater for the increase in vehicular and pedestrian traffic.
  • O.05 Within the 'no development' strip located at the rear of the properties between Tottenham Lane and High Street, Granville (shown in Figure 8.5.14.14 and Figure 8.5.14.15)
  • to make the laneway a safer place;
  • to create passive supervision;
  • to improve landscaping; and
  • to minimise opportunities for graffiti and vandalism

Controls

  • C.01 Plans for Development Applications must show any road widenings, splay corners, road closures and/or 'No Development Strips' that are required by the provisions of this development control plan. This applies where:
  • the property is identified in Figure 8.5.14.14 and Figure 8.5.14.15 of this Section; and
  • the property is not a single dwelling house.

Road Widening

  • C.02 1.5 metres of land shall be dedicated for road widening and/or footpath widening in areas where wider carriageways and footpaths are necessary to cater for the increase in vehicular and pedestrian traffic, as identified in Figure 8.5.14.14.
  • C.03 The developer must meet the cost of constructing the widened road pavement, kerb and gutter and foot paving on the new alignment in accordance with the provisions of this plan.

Splay Corners

  • C.04 In accordance with Figure 8.5.14.13 and Figure 8.5.14.14 showing where splay corners must be provided, the developer must construct and dedicate to Council any splay corner thus identified.

Road Closures

  • C.05 Figure 8.5.14.14, Figure 8.5.14.15 - Road Widening requirements for land fronting Church , and Figure 8.5.14.16 - Frontage requirements - land within Parramatta/Granville show where road closures will be constructed by Council. Council will maintain access to existing developments after the road closures have taken place.
  • C.06 All new developments will not be permitted to use the roads proposed to be closed by the provisions of this plan for access to their land. Access to these sites must be off another road.

Strip

  • C.07 The 'no development' strip is located at the rear of the properties between Tottenham Lane and High Street, shown in Figure 8.5.14.14 and Figure 8.5.14.15 - Road Widening requirements for land fronting Church . The 'no development' strip is to start from the rear of the lots, and be a strip of land 4 metres wide. Landscape this land and keep it free from any structures.
  • C.08 Locate decorative tubular pool style fencing that stands a minimum of 1.5 metres on the boundary of the laneway. Existing conditions are permitted, but the no development strip must be implemented for any future development to be approved.

Rear Access Laneway between High Street and Tottenham Lane

  • C.09 Existing access from the laneway to lots will be continued. Access from the laneway to new developments will be prohibited, with access being from either Raymond Street, High Street, Junction Street or Tottenham Lane.

Implementation

  • C.10 Carry out the construction of the road widening when:
  • Affected sites are developed for any purpose other than for a single dwelling house.
  • Affected sites containing an existing use, other than a single dwelling house, is the subject of an application for further development.
  • Affected sites are the subject of an application for subdivision or strata subdivision.
  • C.11 Complete the works required under this Development Control Plan prior to the release of an occupation certificate by Council.
  • C.12 In the case of all sites, other than those used, or to be used, for a single dwelling house, show the required works on any strata or subdivision plan submitted to Council for approval. Council will hold a bond on the dedication of the subject land.
  • C.18 5 metres of land as shown in Figure 8.5.14.15 - Road Widening requirements for land fronting Church is to be dedicated to Council for the purposes of road widening.

PARRAMATTA CITY CENTRE
